key_insight: This paper shows that GUI agents can learn better task planning by autonomously exploring websites and reusing past mistakes as training signals. The result is a more practical way to improve small open-source multimodal models without relying on expensive proprietary systems.
problem_solved: Small open-source multimodal language models are cost-effective and privacy-preserving, but they often struggle with planning multi-step GUI tasks and generalizing across different websites.
method: Autonomously explores GUI environments to collect planning experiences without heavy human annotation.
Uses hindsight experience utilization to turn failed or suboptimal trajectories into useful learning signals.
Trains task-planning capability so agents can better decompose complex web tasks into executable actions and generalize across sites.
impact: This matters because it offers a scalable path to improve GUI agents using open-source models, making web automation more accessible, private, and cost-efficient. Practitioners get a stronger planning framework for repetitive multi-step tasks across diverse interfaces.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing autonomous exploration -> hindsight relabeling -> planning training -> improved GUI agent
Before/after comparison of task planning quality on unfamiliar websites
Web page flowchart illustrating step-by-step decomposition of a complex GUI task
Icon set for exploration, memory/replay, and cross-site generalization
paper_title: Empowering GUI Agents via Autonomous Experience Exploration and Hindsight Experience Utilization for Task Planning
paper_authors: Tianyi Men, Zhuoran Jin, Pengfei Cao, Yubo Chen, Kang Liu
